column1: # SandboxID device pool — multi-brand REAL-device identity source for `autopif.sh device`
# Each row is one genuine, shipping smartphone whose identity fields were taken
# from real firmware (build.prop dumps on dumps.tadiphone.dev / GitHub device
# trees, cross-checked against vendor spec sheets). No fictional models.
# `autopif.sh device` picks ONE row at random, layers a coherent synthetic
# lifecycle on top (boot count / uptime / "fresh" state derived from the
# device's release date), and writes a verbatim identity.prop-style artifact to
# This is SEPARATE from the default no-arg `fetch` path (Pixel canary), which is
# unchanged. Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored by the reader.
# 15 TAB-separated columns (note: sdk comes BEFORE release):
#   1 brand            ro.product.brand              (real casing: Infinix, OPPO, vivo, samsung, Xiaomi, Redmi, POCO)
#   2 manufacturer     ro.product.manufacturer       (Redmi/POCO -> Xiaomi; Infinix -> INFINIX caps)
#   7 board            ro.board.platform             (SoC-detect anchor; Exynos uses erdXXXX)
#   9 soc_model        ro.soc.model                  (Exynos s5eXXXX; Snapdragon SMXXXX; MediaTek MTXXXX)
#  15 release_date     model market-release month    (YYYY-MM; drives the lifecycle age)
# CAVEAT (vivo rows): public vivo firmware dumps are qssi/mssi ENGINEERING
# recompiles, so `incremental` is the genuine ro.build.version.incremental
# (eng.compil.*) — verifiable and internally consistent with the generated
# fingerprint, but engineering-channel rather than a retail OTA string. Every
